title: Tow Truck – Free Physics Driving Game With a Wobbly Trailer
description: Play Tow Truck free in your browser: hold to drive, release to brake, and tow a trailer full of crates, barrels and sheep to the barn without spilling them.
body: Hold to drive, release to brake. Your little tow truck pulls a trailer on a hinge, and nothing on the trailer is tied down: crates, barrels and a few fluffy sheep slide and bounce with every hill.

A red barn waits every 200 m. Everything still on the trailer when you pass the barn post is delivered, and each item is worth as many points as the barn is far away, so the fourth barn pays twice as much as the second. Then the farmer swaps what you delivered for fresh cargo, plus a bonus item when at least three arrive. Whatever fell off on the way is gone for good, so every item counts. Lose everything, or roll the truck, and the run is over. Don't worry about the sheep: if one falls off it lands on its feet and trots home.
One button, no text, runs of one to three minutes, and it works on phones, tablets, Chromebooks and desktops. New here? Read how to play and the tips to deliver more cargo.

title: How to Play Tow Truck – Controls, Barns and Score
description: Tow Truck controls in one line: hold to drive, release to brake. Learn how the trailer, the barns, the score and the coins work.
body: Tow Truck uses a single input. Hold the mouse button, your finger or the Space bar (Up, Right, W and D also work) to drive forward. Release to brake. In the air, holding tips the truck back and releasing tips it forward.

The trailer is hooked to the back of the truck and swings freely. Its cargo is loose: up to four items on the bed and two stacked on top. The front board is low and the tailgate at the back is even lower, so on steep climbs the load slides backwards. Anything that falls off the trailer is lost. The crate number in the top left corner shows how many items you still carry.

Every 200 m there is a red barn with a striped post. When the trailer passes the post, everything on it is delivered. Your score grows by items × metres: four items at the 400 m barn are worth 1,600 points. You also earn one coin per item.

After each delivery the farmer loads one new item for each one you delivered, plus a bonus item if three or more arrived (up to six). Lost items are not replaced, so the run gets tighter as you go. The bar under the score shows how close the next barn is.

The run ends when the trailer is empty or the truck stays upside down. Your best score, best distance and coins are saved automatically. Coins buy new paint for the truck, new trailers and new cargo in the shop (the bag button on the menu).

title: Tow Truck Tips: Deliver More Cargo to the Barn
description: Practical tips for Tow Truck: how to keep crates, barrels and sheep on the trailer over hills, bumps, ramps and rope bridges.
body: Brake gently. The trailer keeps rolling when you let go and pushes the truck. Short releases are safer than a long stop, which throws the cargo forward.
Ease off before the top of a hill. Coming over a crest at full speed makes the trailer jump and the top items fly off. Let go for a moment and roll over.
Bumps and rope bridges rattle the load. The plank bridges sag in the middle and every plank is a little step. Cross them at a steady medium speed.
Climb in one go. The tailgate is low: stopping halfway up a steep hill lets the cargo slide out of the back. Build speed before the climb and keep the button down.
Ramps are optional. Release before the lip and the truck drops off the end instead of flying. The trailer lands much softer.
Sheep bounce. When they are bumped they hop a little, so a sheep on a shaky trailer can hop right off. Keep it smooth when they are on board.

Later barns are worth more. Each item scores the barn's distance, so one item saved for the 800 m barn is worth four items at the first one. Deliver three or more at a barn and the farmer adds a bonus item. A slow run that keeps going beats a fast run that empties the trailer.

title: Tow Truck FAQ
description: Answers about Tow Truck: is it free, does it save, does it work on mobile and Chromebook, why did my run end, what happens to the sheep.
body: Is it free? Yes, it is free to play in the browser, with no download and no account.
Does it save my progress? Yes. Your best score, your longest distance, your coins and the items you bought in the shop are stored in your browser (or in your CrazyGames account there).
Does it work on phones and Chromebooks? Yes, with touch, mouse or keyboard (Space, Up, Right, W or D), in landscape or portrait.
Why did my run end? Either the trailer was empty before the next barn, or the truck stayed upside down for more than a second.
Do the sheep get hurt? No. A sheep that falls off lands on its feet and runs back to the farm.
How do I get more coins? Deliver cargo (one coin per item), open the game every day for the daily gift, and on some sites you can choose to watch an ad at the end of a run to double that run's coins.
Can I turn the music off? Yes, with the speaker button in the corner.

title: Tow Truck for Schools and Kids – Safe, Short, No Sign-up
description: Tow Truck is a short, text-free farm physics game that works on school Chromebooks: no chat, no purchases, no account, no personal data.
h1: Tow Truck for classrooms and kids
body: Tow Truck is a friendly farm game: a little tow truck carries crates, barrels and sheep to the barn at sunset. There is no violence, no chat, no purchases, no account and no personal data, and the sheep never get hurt.
There is no text in the game, only numbers and pictures, so it works for children who are still learning to read and for students of any language.

It is a hands-on lesson in physics: a trailer on a hinge, loose cargo that slides when you brake, momentum on hills and balance on a sagging bridge. The score is a small piece of maths too: items × metres.
Runs last one to three minutes, which makes it a good reward between tasks. It runs in the browser on Chromebooks, tablets and phones and loads in a couple of seconds (about 1.6 MB in total).
